artifacts.summary: Confirms .projects[<path>].mcpServers is a live, empty, unwritten-to registration surface; identifies the email extension's settings-fragment.json hooks.PreToolUse + provides.hooks pairing as the precedented mechanism for an extension-owned native SessionStart hook; maps all 7 outstanding issues to specific files and confirms task 203's research already named this exact fix as its declined 'Option B'.

memory_candidates.content: An extension can add a native Claude Code SessionStart (or other harness-level) hook without touching core's settings.json or manifest hooks object: declare the script under the extension's own hooks/ directory in provides.hooks, and merge a hooks.<Event> block into the extension's settings-fragment.json. merge.lua's deep_merge/merge_hook_event_array specifically recognizes hook-event arrays ({matcher, hooks} objects) and merges by matcher — appending new hook entries into an existing same-matcher block or appending a new matcher block — never duplicating. Precedent: agent-system/extensions/email/settings-fragment.json's hooks.PreToolUse + hooks/mail-guard.sh. This is distinct from the internal agent-system lifecycle-hook system (manifest.json top-level hooks object, preflight/postflight stages via skill-base.sh) — the two must not be conflated.

~/.claude.json's .projects[<abs-path>].mcpServers is a real, first-class per-project MCP registration surface (Claude Code's 'local scope'), already present as an empty object on every registered project path on this machine. It is distinct from the top-level global mcpServers object and takes precedence over it for that project. Nothing in this repo currently writes to it, but mcp-server-ownership.md already names it as the mechanism a per-project-computed-argument server (like lean-lsp) would need for true multi-project concurrency, as opposed to the single-global-entry model which only one project can correctly use at a time.
